messages.coding.settings.methods-help: In a coding session’s input area, click Skill or type /, read the text and choose. Changing it affects only the next turn; the run record keeps the version used then.
messages.coding.settings.methods-note: Skills are saved in this project and must be chosen in a session after installing. Installing runs no scripts in the package and adds no tool permissions; a skill with the same name is not overwritten.
messages.coding.settings.no-runtimes: The host has not registered any runtime yet
messages.coding.settings.role.writers: Main task reads only; writes in assigned subdirectories are reviewed one by one
messages.coding.settings.runtime.methods-none: Skills: not available in this runtime
messages.coding.settings.runtime.methods-partial: Skills: choose them yourself or let Coding select applicable Skills set to Auto. Their text is read for this turn and stays at the frozen version.
messages.coding.settings.runtime.read-only: Read-only: writes are not connected to the host’s approval
messages.coding.settings.runtime.write: Can read and edit files; writes go through the host’s review.
messages.coding.settings.runtime.write-command: Can read and edit files and run commands; writes and commands go through the host’s review.
messages.coding.skill.coding-diagnose-fix.descrip: Find a reproducible cause first, then make the smallest fix and check both failure and recovery.
messages.coding.skill.coding-diagnose-fix.name: Find and fix a problem
messages.coding.skill.coding-git-delivery.descrip: Check the branch, changes and evidence from checks, and prepare the commit and delivery within the access already granted.
messages.coding.skill.coding-git-delivery.name: Prepare delivery
messages.coding.skill.coding-implement-change.des: Connect the whole user path along the existing structure, checking the differences and when it is done.
messages.coding.skill.coding-review-change.descri: Find problems against the actual code and requirements, separating confirmed risks from items still to verify.
messages.coding.skill.coding-review-change.name: Review changes
messages.coding.slash.label: Commands
messages.coding.start.existing: Your sessions are on the left; open one to carry on.
messages.coding.start.lede: It reads code, proposes a plan, edits files and runs checks; every write and command waits for your review first.
messages.coding.start.title: Write code with an Agent
messages.coding.starter.add-tests: Add a set of unit tests
messages.coding.starter.add-tests-prompt: Add a set of unit tests for the core logic, covering edge cases, and make sure they all pass.
messages.coding.starter.fix-tests-prompt: Run the tests, find why they fail and fix them, then run them again to confirm.
messages.coding.starter.map-project-prompt: Walk me through this project’s main modules and call chains, reading only for now.
messages.coding.starter.review-changes-prompt: Review the current changes for likely bugs and missed edge cases.
messages.coding.step.busy: The earlier step request is still being handled; try again shortly.
messages.coding.step.no-reports: The model hasn’t reported on this step yet.
messages.coding.step.note: A model reporting success does not mean you have accepted it. Check what the original turn actually did and produced before you judge it.
messages.coding.step.run-ended: The run has ended; the step reports keep their states, so check each one.
messages.coding.step.run-running: This turn is still running; you can assess it once it ends, and read the latest reports again meanwhile.
messages.coding.step.saved-accepted: Your acceptance is saved; the model’s reports stay as they were.
messages.coding.step.saved-rework: The rework note is saved; use it to adjust the next plan.
messages.coding.step.see-insert: See the note on the inserted step
messages.coding.step.stale-verdict: This assessment is for an earlier report; check the current version again.
messages.coding.step.state.succeeded: The model reports success; for you to check
messages.coding.step.state.unknown: State can’t be read right now
messages.coding.step.title: Step report and acceptance
messages.coding.step.unreadable: The step’s reports can’t be read right now, so whether it’s done can’t be judged.
messages.coding.sub.assignment: See the task and its access
messages.coding.sub.compare-hint: Tick “Compare” on two sub-tasks to see their conclusions and changes side by side.
messages.coding.sub.look: See the changes and decide whether to integrate
messages.coding.sub.note: The parent task gathers and reviews; a sub-task ending doesn’t mean its result is accepted.
messages.coding.sub.own-usage: This sub-task’s usage: {usage}; not included in the parent’s subtotal.
messages.coding.sub.partial: This sub-task didn’t end normally but changed files in its own directory; the changes may be incomplete, so read the diff before deciding whether to integrate.
messages.coding.sub.rework: Mark for rework and prepare the task
messages.coding.sub.rework-saved: The rework reason is saved and the task is in the input box; it runs only when you send it. The original result is kept.
messages.coding.sub.stop-asked: Asked the original sub-task to stop.
messages.coding.sub.title: Sub-tasks
messages.coding.sub.unreadable: Sub-tasks can’t be read right now: {reason}
messages.coding.sub.verdict-saved: Your assessment of this result is saved.
messages.coding.timeline.check.unreadable: Check result can’t be read right now
messages.coding.tool-hint.denied: This command did not run: how it is written, or the extra access it asks for, is against the rules.
messages.coding.tool-hint.secret: Part of the new content looks like a secret key, so nothing was written and no change was proposed for review. Keep keys out of project files: put them in the key store or an environment variable and have it use a reference.
messages.coding.tool-hint.stale: The file changed after it was read, so this edit was not written over it; it needs to read the file again before editing.
messages.coding.tool.unavailable: This page is not available right now
messages.coding.turn-changes.digest: SHA-256 of the content on disk after the write: {digest}
messages.coding.turn-changes.note: What the write receipts recorded, not what the model says. Files changed by commands aren’t listed here.
messages.coding.turn-changes.rewind-label: Preview rewinding to before {path} was written
messages.coding.turn.material-named: Attached material: {name} (given to the model as reference data, not instructions)
messages.coding.usage-line.compaction-incomplete: , though some tidying is missing full usage
messages.coding.usage-line.incomplete: Usage is incomplete or includes estimates: {reason}
messages.coding.view.board-title: This session’s plan, each step and its sub-tasks; you can adjust them
messages.coding.view.label: Main area view
messages.coding.welcome.lede: Just describe the goal. I read the code before touching anything, and every write and command waits for your review first.
messages.coding.welcome.title: What do you want to get done?
messages.coding.workspace.choose-first: Choose a granted workspace to begin
messages.coding.workspace.choose-needed: Choose or link a working directory
messages.coding.workspace.confirm: Link the new directory to this project as the task workspace.
messages.coding.workspace.confirm-needed: Confirm linking this directory to the project
messages.coding.workspace.files-git-unchanged: {reason}. Files and Git still show the previous directory.
messages.coding.workspace.note: Used from the next turn; a task already running keeps its workspace.
messages.coding.workspace.path-placeholder: An absolute path on this computer
messages.coding.workspace.switch-failed: Could not switch the project’s current directory
messages.coding.workspace.switch-failed-why: Could not switch the project’s current directory: {reason}
messages.coding.workspace.title: Choose a workspace
messages.coding.workspace.unavailable: The original workspace is not available right now; choose again
messages.coding.workspace.unbound: This project has no workspace directory bound yet
messages.coding.worktrees.needs-writing: Choose Edit files or Run first
messages.coding.worktrees.note: Creates a separate directory and local branch from the main repository’s current commit. Creating it and granting it to the project are reviewed first; with uncommitted changes nothing is branched, so none of the current changes are left out.
messages.coding.worktrees.note-parallel: Use one as the next turn’s workspace, or tick directories and fill in a parallel split. After saving the split, choose Parallel writing and send; every change and command is still reviewed. When a sub-task ends, see and pick its results in the results area, and bring them back to the main workspace through another review.
messages.coding.worktrees.split-saved: The split is saved; it starts once you choose Parallel writing and send the task.
messages.coding.worktrees.title: Separate worktrees
messages.coding.worktrees.used-next: The next turn uses the chosen separate directory; the original task and the main workspace stay as they are.
messages.coding.writers.busy: The earlier directory action is still being handled; open this again shortly
messages.coding.writers.choose-first: Choose a coding session and an authorized main workspace first
messages.coding.writers.integrate: Bring back into the main workspace
messages.coding.writers.none: No separate worktrees are ready for this repository yet.
messages.coding.writers.problem: Can no longer be used as a separate worktree: {reason}. The directory and its contents are left as they are; check them and deal with them yourself.
messages.coding.writers.saved-gone: A saved split directory isn’t available right now: {id}
messages.coding.writers.task: This directory’s task and done condition
